title: Magnetic parts tray
prompt: Magnetic parts tray for the workbench: an 80 × 40 × 16 mm block centred on the origin on Z = 0, with a 64 × 24 mm pocket 10 mm deep in the top (a 6 mm floor). In the underside, two flat-bottomed pockets for Ø8 × 3 mm magnets (Ø8.2, 3.2 deep) at x = ±30 on the centre line. A Ø3 drain hole drilled up from the underside into the pocket at the centre. Two M4 mounting holes through the pocket floor at x = ±20 with a loose fit so the tray can be adjusted, and two pilot holes for M3 self-tapping lid screws (the M3 tap drill, 8 mm deep, not threaded) in the top of the end walls at x = ±36. Make the magnet pockets and every hole hole features.

hidden_tests.description: Evaluates cleanly and every body is a valid closed solid
Two Ø8.2 × 3.2 blind magnet pockets drilled up from the underside
The magnet pockets open in the underside (z = 0) at x = ±30
Only the two pilot holes end in a drill point: the magnet pockets (and the drain, drilled to the floor) are flat
The Ø3 drain is drilled up from the underside and stops at the pocket floor (6 mm)
The drain is on the centre axis (a through-going hole has no geometric side; how it was drilled is the drain test's)
Two M4 loose-fit (Ø4.8, ISO 273 coarse) through holes
The mounting holes go through the pocket floor at x = ±20
Two M3 tap-drill pilots (Ø2.5, 8 deep, no cosmetic thread) drilled down into the end walls
The pilots open in the top of the end walls at x = ±36

notes: Magnets 2·π·4.1²·3.2 = 337.98 (flat floors; a 118° drill point would add 2·43.4); drain π·1.5²·6 = 42.41 (drilled up_to the pocket floor, so it opens into the pocket); M4 loose Ø4.8 through the 6 mm floor: 2·π·2.4²·6 = 217.15; M3 tap Ø2.5 × 8 with a 118° point: 2·(39.27 + 1.23) = 81.00. The drain is a flipped hole on XY (XY's normal points into the part) or, equivalently, a hole on the bottom face; its depth is up_to the pocket floor. The oracle warns HOLE_BREAKS_THROUGH on that up_to hole and Forge does not: under SPEC §8.4 that is a CODE_MISMATCH between the engines, pending a contract ruling on §6.5 (the open W5 question, forge-ops hole/mod.rs); the real-engine differential reports it apart as an open contract question (evals v1/diff.ts OPEN_CONTRACT_QUESTIONS), and no hidden test reads warnings. Construction: magnets, drain, loose_mounts, pilots read the hole features the prompt asks for (no geometry equivalent in the report), so a correct part built otherwise fails only those tests.
